findings.problem: BatchWorkflow has no typestate enum. Status, validation flags, and timestamp are flat booleans/strings instead of an explicit state machine with valid transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct any combination of fields including impossible states like status=draft with is_sent=true, or status=validated with is_validated=false. No invariant enforcement exists at the type level.
findings.fix: Replace status/is_validated/is_sent/sent_at_epoch_ms with a single BatchStatus enum (e.g. Draft, Validated, Sent) whose variants own their lifecycle data. Use a smart constructor or Result-returning parse fn as the only path to BatchWorkflow.

findings.problem: status: String allows arbitrary strings including invalid lifecycle values. Status must be an enum to prevent impossible domain states.
findings.failure_mode: Callers set status to any string ("sent", "SENT", "deleted", ""). No compile-time guarantee that status reflects a valid lifecycle stage. mark_sent sets it to "sent" but callers can set it to anything else afterwards.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with `status: BatchStatus` enum (Draft, Validated, Sent). Remove is_validated and is_sent as redundant booleans. Enum variant owns the lifecycle data.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool encode lifecycle as independent booleans, creating impossible state combinations that the type system cannot prevent.
findings.failure_mode: States like (is_validated=true, is_sent=true, status="draft") or (is_validated=false, is_sent=true) are impossible in the domain but fully representable. mark_sent does not set is_validated, so callers can send without validating.
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single typestate enum. Each enum variant represents one valid lifecycle stage. Variant data (e.g. sent timestamp) lives in the variant, not as separate fields.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is decoupled from the state machine. The Option exists independently of whether the batch is actually in the Sent state.
findings.failure_mode: A batch in Draft status can have sent_at_epoch_ms = Some(12345) which is semantically wrong. Conversely, a Sent batch could have None. The timestamp should only exist when the Sent variant is active.
findings.fix: Move sent timestamp into the BatchStatus::Sent variant: `BatchStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`. Remove the standalone Option field entirely.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no newtype wrapper, validation, or domain constraints. Empty strings, duplicated IDs, and malformed IDs are all allowed.
findings.failure_mode: Callers create BatchWorkflow with id="", id="   ", or duplicate IDs. No uniqueness or format enforcement at any layer. The domain rule for valid IDs is invisible in the type.
findings.fix: Replace with `id: BatchId` newtype containing a validated String or a fixed-size byte array. Provide a parse constructor `BatchId::from_str(s) -> Result<BatchId, ParseError>`.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates status (String) and is_sent (bool) directly instead of performing a typed state transition. No validation, no state machine, no error on invalid transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can call mark_sent on a Draft, Validated, or already-Sent batch with no guard. mark_sent also does not set sent_at_epoch_ms, creating a Sent batch without a timestamp. Callers can call mark_sent multiple times with no observable difference.
findings.fix: Replace with `fn try_transition_to_sent(item: BatchWorkflow) -> Result<BatchWorkflow, TransitionError>` that validates preconditions (e.g. must be Validated first) and returns a new state via the typestate enum.

findings.problem: Raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors. BatchWorkflow fields (String, bool, Option<u64>) are directly constructible by callers, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: No constructor, parser, or factory exists. Any code can `BatchWorkflow { id: String::new(), status: "anything", is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None }` and the compiler accepts it. Domain invariants are unenforced at every call site.
findings.fix: Add a private struct or private fields with a single public constructor `BatchWorkflow::new(id: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError>` that validates all invariants. Or use a typestate enum with smart constructors on each variant.

residual_risk: Review is static analysis only. All fields are public with no type-level invariants. The typestate pattern must be implemented and tested to close these violations. Without typestate, the domain is fully representable in illegal states with zero compiler protection.
